title: Cylindrical rod
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. On the first face, draw the first loop as a circle centered at coordinates [0.0188, 0.0188] with a radius of 0.0188. Draw the second loop as another circle centered at the same coordinates but with a smaller radius of 0.015. Scale the entire sketch by a factor of 0.0375. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same vector. Extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Finally, create a new solid body from the extruded sketch. The final dimensions of the cylindrical rod with a rectangular cross-section at one end will be 0.0375 units in length, 0.0375 units in width, and 0.75 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the cross-section
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0188, 0.0188)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0188)         # Outer circle
    .circle(0.015)          # Inner circle
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the rod
rod = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Final model
r = rod

import cadquery as cq

# Dimensions
outer_d = 0.0376
inner_d = 0.0280
length = 0.7500

# Create the tube: hollow cylinder along Z
r = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .circle(outer_d / 2.0)
    .circle(inner_d / 2.0)
    .extrude(length)
)

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

OD = 0.0376
L = 0.7500
WALL = 0.0050
ID = OD - 2 * WALL

r = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .circle(OD / 2)
    .extrude(L)
    .faces(">Z")
    .workplane()
    .hole(ID)
)
